prompt:
Complete the layered configuration compiler migration in this std-only/offline Cargo crate. Preserve public types/functions, wire formats, and CLI commands; replace the legacy ancestor replay, exact-key deletes and textual interpolation with the full pipeline below across domain and adapter modules. Add regression tests. No dependencies or environment/network lookups.

MODEL: model.rs specifies signatures. Rules describe exact flat paths (a and a.b may both exist); path syntax is dot-separated [a-z][a-z0-9_]* segments. Layer names match [a-z][a-z0-9_-]*. Kind is Text{nonempty}, Integer{inclusive min,max}, Boolean, or List{inclusive min,max item counts}. Rule.required is presence, not truthiness; Rule.secret controls information flow and output redaction. Layer operations are zero-indexed in operations (parents declarations are NOT operations). Origin is layer name plus that zero-based operation index.

COMPILATION/PRECEDENCE: (1) schema::index scans rules in declaration order: invalid-path:<path>, duplicate-rule:<path>, invalid-rule:<path> for inverted Integer/List bounds. Then constraints in input order: invalid-constraint:<index> unless Requires refers to two known paths, or Exclusive has >=2 distinct known paths. (2) graph::validate validates the ENTIRE layer collection, including unreachable layers. Scan declarations for invalid-layer:<name>, duplicate-layer:<name>. Then layers sorted by name and parents in declared order: missing-parent:<layer>-><parent> before duplicate-parent:<layer>-><parent>. Detect GLOBAL cycles by lexicographic Kahn elimination; cycle:<smallest remaining layer name> (including downstream nodes). (3) validation::operations scans ALL layers sorted by name, ops in original order: invalid-path:<path>, unknown-path:<path>, operation-type:<path>. Set requires a non-List rule; SetList/Append/Remove require List. Delete accepts a prefix matching at least one rule at self or dot-delimited descendant; otherwise unknown-path. Validate even overridden/unreachable operations. (4) unknown-layer:<target>. (5) linearize selected target: depth-first postorder, parents in DECLARED order, each ancestor exactly once globally (diamond ancestors never replay). (6) apply operations. (7) required checks by sorted path. (8) expand interpolation for every present path in sorted order. (9) type validation by sorted path. (10) constraints in declaration order. All failures are Error, not panics, for malformed inputs covered here. Inputs are immutable; repeated compiles cannot leak state across targets.

MERGE/TOMBSTONES: Set and SetList replace value and reset contributors=[this origin]. Lists are stable-unique preserving first occurrence at SetList and after every Append; Remove removes all matching raw strings, before interpolation. Append initializes a missing/deleted list as empty; Remove of a missing/deleted value is missing-value:<path>. Every Append/Remove, including an empty/no-effect operation, sets origin to this op and appends its origin to contributors. A Delete removes the exact path AND every dot-delimited descendant currently present, never prefix lookalikes (delete net leaves network). It records tombstones[prefix]=origin; later deletes at that EXACT prefix replace that record, but all other prefix records remain. These are historical deletion audit records: they survive resurrection, including later Set/Append, and do NOT mask values written later. Repeated/overlapping prefix deletes are valid even when values are absent. Parent order and operation order both affect results; tombstones are not final filtering instructions.

INTERPOLATION: Resolve AFTER all selected merges, against FINAL present raw values. Scalar strings and every list item support ${path}; referenced values must be scalar, even when the referring field is a list. Resolve transitively with memoization and cycle detection; values are scanned by sorted path, strings left-to-right, list items in order. Encountering an active path yields interpolation-cycle:<that referenced path>. Unknown/deleted references yield reference:<immediate referring path>-><reference>; referring to a list yields reference-type:<referrer>-><reference>. An unterminated ${ yields interpolation:<referrer>. $$ emits one literal $ and suppresses interpolation for that pair ($${x} is literal ${x}); all other $ and Unicode chars are literal. Output from a reference is NOT rescanned for new escapes/placeholders. Empty/invalid reference names are simply missing references, not schema parse errors. A public rule referencing a secret rule fails secret-flow:<referrer>-><reference> BEFORE resolving that reference. Secret rules may reference public or secret. Transitive flow is checked on every edge. Resolved.references is the sorted DISTINCT union of all direct and transitive reference paths, excluding escaped literals. List items are stable-deduplicated AGAIN after interpolation. Interpolation leaves origin/contributors unchanged. References use the expanded RAW scalar, before type canonicalization (an integer raw 001 is referenced as 001).

TYPES/CONSTRAINTS: nonempty text rejects only empty string, not whitespace. Integer syntax is -?[0-9]+ (no plus, whitespace, decimal point, overflow); parse i64, then inclusive bounds; typed values canonicalize numerically. Boolean accepts only exact true/false. List min/max apply after interpolation/dedup. All type failures are type:<path>. A required missing final value is required:<path>. Requires{when,path} checks presence only, so false/empty when values still require path; fail requires:<when>-><path>. Exclusive permits at most one PRESENT path; fail exclusive:<comma-joined sorted present paths>. Tombstones do not count as presence.

WIRE PARSERS: Skip whitespace-only lines and lines beginning # at column zero; otherwise do not trim. Physical error line numbers are 1-based. Schema lines are path|KIND|required-or-optional|secret-or-public. KIND is text, nonempty, bool, int:MIN:MAX, list:MIN:MAX; integer bounds use the same signed decimal syntax; list bounds unsigned decimal usize, no signs. Also !requires|when|path and !exclusive|comma-paths. Bad syntax is schema-parse:<line>; semantic invalid bounds/names/constraints defer to compilation. Layer text uses [name] section headers, optional parents=a,b at most once BEFORE any operations, then set|path|scalar, list|path|comma-items, append|path|comma-items, remove|path|comma-items, delete|prefix. Empty comma-items means empty list; otherwise preserve empty members and whitespace. Empty parent list means no parents. Ops before a header, duplicate/late parents, wrong arity/unknown op are layer-parse:<line>. Duplicate section names are semantic duplicate-layer errors, not merged. No escaping of |, commas or newlines in wire values; direct model APIs accept arbitrary strings. Parse does not perform semantic validation.

ADAPTERS: service::compile_text parses schema then layers then compiles; returns (Schema,Compiled). render_text renders that result. render::compiled emits no terminal newline: layers=ordered,names then values sorted by path as value|path|text-or-int-or-bool-or-list|serialized|origin_layer:index|refs=sorted,paths, followed by sorted deleted|prefix|origin_layer:index. Lists serialize comma-joined, integers canonical decimal, booleans lowercase. redact=true substitutes [REDACTED] for the entire serialized value of a secret rule, but never alters stored typed values/provenance; redact=false reveals it. render::value returns (kind tag, serialized value). batch::compile_text parses once, compiles each target independently in caller order, joins renders with newline--newline; returns first error (an empty target list still parses syntax). explain::path returns origin=L:I;contributors=L:I,...;references=paths for a PRESENT path only, else not-found:<path>, with no secret value leakage. diff::between compares only typed values across the union of keys, sorted by path; omit provenance-only changes; include additions/removals as Option<Value>.

CLI: compile SCHEMA LAYERS TARGET [--reveal] renders with redaction by default; explain SCHEMA LAYERS TARGET PATH uses explain; batch SCHEMA LAYERS TARGET... accepts >=1 target and redacts each result. Success stdout is adapter output plus one newline; any error stderr is Display plus newline and exit code 2. Keep the executable corpus; hidden tests exercise public model helpers, interpolation/provenance, validation precedence, independently compiled branches, parsers, all adapters and CLI.
